# Local dungeon arch shape test

This is an isolated geometry test of the existing local `CL3D/2mini`
checkpoint and Python environment. It does not alter the pipeline, original
penguin demo, or game scene.

## Reproduce

From `/Users/theochernin/Projects/CherninLab3D/CL3D`:

```sh
../.venv/bin/python ../tests/dungeon_arch_01/run_shape_test.py \
  ../tests/dungeon_arch_01/input.png \
  --output ../tests/dungeon_arch_01/arch-v2.glb
```

The runner refuses to overwrite an existing output. Defaults: MPS, float16,
50 sampling steps, 384 extraction resolution, CPU random generator seed
20261024. `arch.json` records actual timing, counts, bounds, and memory
allocated after inference. These memory figures are not peak measurements.

## Reference generation

`input.png` is a native built-in ImageGen output, copied without alteration
from the tool's generated-images directory. It has a transparent background.
It is a reconstruction reference, not a rendered result of the 3D model.

Final prompt:

> Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: single-object image-to-3D reconstruction input for a realistic folk-horror dungeon game. Generate ONE freestanding ancient broken stone doorway arch, isolated on a genuinely transparent background. A grounded, physically plausible medieval rubble-stone architectural fragment: two unequal substantial piers with chipped bases support one complete intact pointed Gothic arch. The opening is fully empty, unobstructed and clearly visible through to transparency. A little ragged ruined masonry rises outside the arch, with an asymmetric broken top silhouette, but the load-bearing arch itself remains continuous. The object is a compact modular wall fragment, about 3.2 metres tall, 2.7 metres wide, and 0.55 metres thick. Camera at human eye height in a gentle three-quarter front view, about 15 degrees off frontal, so the entire opening and the thick inner stone reveal are clearly visible; no extreme perspective or lens distortion. Full object, both feet visible, generous 10 percent transparent margin. Materials: varied individually weathered grey-brown limestone blocks, larger carved voussoirs at the arch, small irregular stones in piers, pale eroded lime mortar, sparse moss low on bases, chips and clear structural cracks. Medium-sized relief and distinct stone silhouettes, not just photographic micro-noise. Realistic physically based sculpted game asset, natural diffuse studio lighting with mild directional shading, clear midtones. No floor, no surrounding dungeon, no scenic background, no enclosed black backdrop inside the doorway, no doors or bars, no characters, no foliage strands, no text, no pedestal, no disconnected rubble, no additional props, no watermark. Make this visually useful for reconstructing geometry rather than a cinematic scene.

## Review criteria

- The doorway remains open in 3D.
- Both piers and the overhead arch stay connected.
- The mesh retains depth, chipped silhouette, and large stone relief.
- Exported geometry is finite, has valid indices, and imports for rendering.
- Clay previews use neutral review lighting/materials added only in Blender;
  they do not demonstrate generated textures or game lighting.

## Observed result

The first run completed on this Mac: 10.71 seconds to load, followed by
41.39 seconds for shape inference and mesh extraction. The exported GLB
contains 320,658 vertices and 641,376 triangles. It has finite coordinates,
valid indices, consistent winding, zero open boundary edges, and zero
nonmanifold edges. There are three closed connected components: one large
arch and two small islands. Fifteen triangles have area below 1e-12 in the
normalized coordinates.

The front, side, back, and three-quarter Blender renders confirm that the
doorway remains open and the module has actual depth. The model retains
the large masonry silhouette and trim, but stones are rounded, fine chips
and cracks are largely absent, and unwanted voids appear near the bases.
The model needs cleanup and simplification before game use.

This export contains only positions and triangle indices. It has no UVs,
materials, embedded textures, or stored normals. The renders show clay
geometry only. No game import or character collision test was performed.

Outputs: `arch.glb`, `arch.json`, `mesh-audit.json`, `generation.log`, and
four PNGs under `renders/`.
